headline: Highest risk is medium: no documented shared channel, but both docs-only agents could still be composed through external workflows, creating limited prompt, leakage, and compliance uncertainty.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel, filesystem, clipboard, or MCP surface is documented for either agent. agent_a is a non-runnable content-writing repo with empty io_surfaces; agent_b is a data-engineering project with network_egress none and empty io_surfaces. Without a bridge, prompt injection is not a plausible pairwise pathway.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is added between the agents, re-evaluate injection risk.
IF either agent begins parsing the other's raw text as instructions, the pathway becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated from shared copy-paste workflows.
Do not connect them to a common MCP server.
Review any future integration for provenance tagging.
requires-engineering: add explicit trust boundaries if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile shows sensitive data classes touched, shared storage, or outbound inference uploads. agent_a touches no data_classes_touched and agent_b also touches none; agent_b explicitly has network_egress none. With no documented shared workspace, leakage is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is later pointed at a shared workspace containing sensitive files, leakage risk changes.
IF agent_b gains outbound egress or file-upload behavior, reassess exposure.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory.
Confirm agent_b remains network-isolated.
Avoid mounting the same workspace into both agents.
requires-engineering: add DLP or access controls if shared storage is introduced.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write-capable surfaces are documented. agent_a has empty capabilities and io_surfaces, and agent_b only documents network_egress none. With no filesystem, git, database, or OAuth write scope shown for either agent, capability conflict is not evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or mutable resource, conflict risk becomes plausible.
IF either agent receives git or database write scopes, reassess for contention.
mitigations: Do not grant shared write access by default.
Keep mutable resources single-owner.
Document any future write scopes before deployment.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutation is required.

D_cascading_error.rationale: There is no documented pipeline where agent_a's output becomes agent_b's authoritative input, and neither profile shows downstream action-taking authority. agent_a is a content-writing repo, while agent_b is a data-engineering project with no runnable or action fields. The pairwise cascade pathway is therefore unsupported.
conditions: IF agent_a output is later fed into agent_b without verification, cascading error risk appears.
IF agent_b is given action authority based on agent_a text, reassess at higher severity.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between outputs and actions.
Do not auto-ingest agent_a text into agent_b pipelines.
Require schema validation for any handoff.
requires-engineering: add provenance checks for future chaining.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented. Both profiles are docs-only open-source projects with empty data_classes_touched, so there is no evidenced compliance-sensitive data flow between them. The other agent is not cited separately because no compliance-bearing pathway is shown.
conditions: IF either agent is deployed to process regulated data, compliance review is required.
IF a jurisdictional or retention mismatch is introduced in deployment, reassess.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pair.
Document any future data residency requirements.
Review retention settings before deployment.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement if regulated data is introduced.
